subject: Bridgeport: service reconciliation & response plan
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bridgeport.com>, Bridgeport SRE <sre@bridgeport.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Bridgeport: service reconciliation & response plan

Elena / Bridgeport SRE team,

First, I want to apologize for the disruption you experienced on 2028-06-03. We recognize the impact this caused to Bridgeport’s production traffic and user-facing flows, and we take full responsibility for the regression.

This thread is the start of our customer-facing reconciliation: a concise RCA summary, a reproducible timeline, and concrete action items with owners and delivery dates. Attached are the working artifacts we will finalize for you (bridgeport_rca.pdf, bridgeport_timeline.csv, remediation_action_items.xlsx). We will also post a read-only folder with logs and checksums to the Drive link below once validations complete.

High-level summary (one paragraph): 
- What happened: Several customer inference requests returned incorrect completions or 502 errors for a ~45 minute window during the 06:14–07:00 UTC period on 2028-06-03. The event was caused by a regression introduced in a recent kernel rollout that interacted with our multi-tenant KV cache invalidation logic.
- Immediate impact: ~2.1% error rate against Bridgeport traffic at peak; automated retries caused modest increase in downstream latency.
- Customer-facing mitigation: We performed a targeted rollback of the kernel change within 30 minutes of detection and applied a hotfix to disable the new code path for Bridgeport traffic.

Next: I will send a short technical RCA and an owner/action table in the next message (today EOD PT). For transparency we will include: the timeline, the code diff, audit extracts, and planned controls to prevent recurrence.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments (working copies): bridgeport_rca.pdf (draft), bridgeport_timeline.csv (raw), remediation_action_items.xlsx (owner matrix)
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bridgeport.com>

Date: 2028-06-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridgeport: service reconciliation & response plan

Thanks, Lauren.

Appreciate the prompt acknowledgement. A few asks from our side:
- We need a short technical RCA suitable for our engineering leadership (what failed, why the rollback was necessary, and why this slipped past pre-deploy checks).
- A definitive timeline of events (we will reconcile with our own SLO alerts).
- Evidence of audit logs and request traces for the affected window (hashed tokens are fine).
- Bridgeport Procurement is copied — we will expect a proposed compensation/credit for the customer impact and a summary we can use in our vendor risk registry.

Can you commit to delivering the RCA + timeline and a list of action owners by EOD PT tomorrow? Also please include the contact for any follow-up SOC 2 or compliance questions.

- Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, Bridgeport Financial
elena.morales@bridgeport.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bridgeport.com>, Bridgeport SRE <sre@bridgeport.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-06T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridgeport: service reconciliation & response plan

Elena — thank you, and understood. Below is the customer-facing RCA summary and the committed action table. I’m keeping this concise; attachments include the full timeline (bridgeport_timeline.csv) and a downloadable artifact pack at the Drive link.

Executive RCA (concise):
Root cause: During a staged rollout of an optimized kernel path intended to reduce long-context memory utilization, an interaction with our multi-tenant KV cache invalidation produced inconsistent cache state for a small number of concurrent batches. The inconsistent state manifested as key-misalignment between requests and KV lookups for affected tenants, which produced wrong-token completions and, in several cases, runtime errors (502).
Contributing factors: 
- The rollout introduced a code path that bypassed a legacy checksum guard for cache entries when certain padding conditions occurred.
- Our pre-deploy integration tests did not include a cross-tenant concurrency pattern that reproduces the exact ordering observed in production.
- Monitoring alerted on elevated error rates, but the initial signal was de-prioritized due to coincident noise from an unrelated backend job; that slowed diagnosis by ~18 minutes.

What we did to remediate (short):
1) Immediate rollback of the new kernel path for all Bridgeport-serving instances (completed within 30 minutes of escalation).
2) Emergency hotfix to re-enable checksum verification and additional guards; hotfix deployed to Bridgeport traffic only.
3) Extended tracing and persisted hashes for the affected window; copies uploaded to Drive link.

Action items and owners (delivery commitments):
- Deliver final RCA PDF and raw timeline (Lauren) — 2028-06-06 EOD PT (attached draft delivered).
- Hotfix hardening + unit tests for checksum guard (Dylan) — target 2028-06-09.
- Add cross-tenant concurrency test to pre-deploy CI and gate (Kimberly) — target 2028-06-16.
- Audit log extract & SOC 2 control mapping for your vendor registry (Kimberly) — target 2028-06-12.
- Proposal for service credit (Commercial) — draft to Procurement by 2028-06-08 (I’ve looped sales via separate channel).

Safety controls we will implement immediately:
- Tenant isolation flag that pins Bridgeport traffic to the conservative cache path until the new kernel passes extended tests.
- 90-day retention of request traces for Bridgeport (scan-and-hash mode) and an automated digest to be provided weekly for 30 days.

Artifacts provided now (working):
- bridgeport_rca.pdf (draft; includes code diff and short timeline)
- bridgeport_timeline.csv (timestamped events and detection markers)
- remediation_action_items.xlsx (owner matrix)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1BridgeRCA (contains logs + checksums)

We will also schedule a 30-minute technical readout tomorrow to walk through the timeline and controls. Proposed time: 2028-06-10 11:00 PT. Please confirm availability.

Best,
Lauren

On the SOC 2/compliance point: Kimberly Park (cc’d) will own the evidence pack and will provide a mapping of the incident artifacts to relevant SOC 2 controls by 2028-06-12. For immediate questions, kimberly.park@redwood.com is the contact.
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bridgeport.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-07T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridgeport: service reconciliation & response plan

Elena, Lauren — quick follow up with the artifacts I promised.

I’ve uploaded the final sanitized audit extract and the request-hash bundle for the affected window to the Drive folder (same link as above). The bundle contains: 
- request_trace_extract_20280603_hashes.json (SHA256 hashed request ids and timestamps)
- runtime_error_dump_06140300.log (sanitized)
- kernel_diff_rollback.patch (the lines rolled back during emergency remediation)

Status updates on actions: 
- Hotfix hardening: code branch created; CI validations added; production preflight tests running. ETA for gated rollout to general traffic: 2028-06-09. We will not re-enable the fast path for Bridgeport until we complete the cross-tenant concurrency suite.
- Audit & SOC 2 pack: Kimberly is preparing the mapping and will deliver the evidence pack by 2028-06-12.
- Compensation: we have circulated a draft credit proposal to Procurement and will share the final draft by 2028-06-08.

Next steps: please confirm if the proposed readout on 2028-06-10 at 11:00 PT works for your team. If you prefer earlier, we can carve a 20-minute slot tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com
